notes: Second sweep of 2026-10-31 (sweeps/2026-10-31-b, run head 74112b4, uncommitted false): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript reads SKILL.md, the input and references/ex_unit.md with Read, once each, before writing, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md) is met in 5 of 5. Graded against the previous sweep's grades (sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/log-tests-*.json, at 0814e8d).

git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches SKILL.md ("One expression per line, and tabular clauses" gains the for sentences; "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" loses "A `for` always takes `do ... end`"), references/macros.md and references/processes.md. ex_unit.md is unchanged, so all five graded rules are graded to the 2026-10-31 standard. No run writes a for, macro or process, so no changed sentence decides any verdict or any other_violations entry.

All five graded rules are clean in 5 of 5. All five runs use async: true with no Logger.configure, Process.register or application env; haiku-2's top-level Application.ensure_all_started(:logger) (line 2) changes no global state the tests share and, as in 2026-10-22-c, is a script line, not a test body. Assert with patterns: opus-1 and sonnet-1 put the call on the left of ==; sonnet-2 uses that and patterns; haiku-2 asserts patterns on the result it took from with_log; haiku-1 compares that result on the left of ==, the "result bound a line earlier" case the rule's == sentence allows, as haiku-2 was graded in 2026-10-31; the only bare matches are the with_log tuple destructures, which cannot fail. Gateways: opus-1 (nested FakeGateway) and haiku-1 (nested FakeGateway) use one behaviour module answering by token; haiku-2, sonnet-1 (nested) and sonnet-2 (top-level Payments.ChargerTest.*) use one module per outcome.

One judgment call on a shape no earlier sweep has: haiku-2 line 32, describe "charge/3 logging". I graded it clean. The rule says to name a block "after the function under test, or after a condition its tests share", and its first test, that a failure says which function it is about, is met. Its topic sentence ("names a topic and promises nothing") is written for blocks "named after a condition, or after a requirement"; this block is named after the function, and plain describe "charge/3", which also promises nothing, is allowed, so the added word cannot make it worse. If the sentence is meant to forbid a topic word added to a function name, this is one violation and the Haiku tier of this rule becomes violated, and the sentence should say so. The other four runs use describe "charge/3" (opus-1) or charge/3 plus a condition (haiku-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), the shapes 2026-10-31 graded clean. Test names all name the value returned or what was logged; none has the "returns :ok" shape.

Per sentence of the capture_log rule, runs violating: capture_log/2 or with_log/2 rather than a handler, StringIO or backend, 0 of 5; formatter options for format and metadata, 0 of 5 (opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 pass :format, :metadata and :colors; haiku-2 passes :metadata on the default format in its declined test, and uses option-less with_log for the unavailable and success tests, which assert level text only); async: true, 0 of 5; wrap every call that logs, 0 of 5 (sonnet-1 lines 41, 62, 86 and sonnet-2 lines 43, 65, 90 wrap return-value tests in an option-less capture_log; haiku-1 ignores the log with _log in its return-value tests; opus-1 and haiku-2 assert return values alongside their log checks); primary-level and crash-report sentences, not exercised in 5 of 5. Success-case absence: opus-1 refutes its request id in a level: :warning capture, as opus-1 did in 2026-10-23, with a comment giving the reason (other async modules can log during the capture); sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 assert an empty level: :warning capture; haiku-2 asserts an info line and refutes every level from warning up; haiku-1 asserts an info line and refutes [warning] and [error], leaving out critical, alert and emergency, as the Haiku runs did in 2026-10-23; all met the check.

Outside the case's list, two entries, both under sentences unchanged since 0814e8d. haiku-1 line 86 is a 79-character case clause kept on one line; the rule's "a clause whose pattern, `->` and body pass about 70 characters after the indentation goes to two lines even when it fits in 98" decides it, as in 2026-10-31 library-client-baseline (75 and 79 characters). haiku-2 lines 52-54 and 65-67 put a one-expression fn body below its head where the clause is 40 characters and the call is 54; "A `fn` body is laid out like any other body: one expression stays on the head's line" decides it, as in 2026-10-31 ecto-phoenix-baseline sonnet-2 lines 133-135. haiku-2 lines 37-39 are not listed: on one line they pass 98 characters.

A close call left out of other_violations: sonnet-1 lines 41-43, 62-64 and 86-88 put a one-expression fn body (an assert comparison) below its head where the one-line form fits in 98 (89, 95 and 96 characters). Their clauses, fn, `->` and body, are 66, 72 and 73 characters, within a few characters of the rule's "about 70", the band in which 2026-10-31 order-report-skill held a 71-character clause; the -> rule's "A single-clause `fn` passed as an argument reads the same way" lets a clause past 70 go below, and the sibling captures in the same file (lines 50, 71, 95) cannot fit on one line, so the file keeps one layout. The readability section calls this "a reading heuristic, not a measure" and says "the surrounding code" counts. If the line is drawn at exactly 70, lines 41-43 alone would be listed. No other run has a one-expression fn body below its head that fits on the line: opus-1 and sonnet-2 are past 98 on one line, and haiku-1 keeps its fns on one line.

Also not counted, to the 2026-10-31 standard: "Name a step instead of wrapping an expression" for the formatter's wraps after == and = (sonnet-2 lines 44-45, 54-55, 66-67, 76-77, 91-92, 101-102; haiku-1 lines 29-30 and the like), which hold one comparison or one call with no inner step a name would explain; sonnet-2's charge/3 options stay inline as a trailing keyword list. opus-1, sonnet-1 and haiku-2 bind opts first and do not wrap, and those bindings build a list rather than rename a value. Not reported, as before: `result` as a variable name (haiku-1, haiku-2), which ex_unit.md's own `{result, log} = with_log(...)` uses, and gateway modules without @moduledoc false (opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) in an .exs script that builds no docs. haiku-1's log_line/2 uses flunk with a case on Enum.find, one construct, not nested. No with, pipeline or multi-clause function outside the gateway doubles, whose do: clauses form a table.

Tests were run from copies in the grader scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each with ExUnit's random seed: every file passed every time (opus-1 and haiku-2 3 tests; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 6 each) with no compiler warning and no log line printed. All five pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json. Each file was run against the five mutants of the earlier sweeps (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error): every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so no log assertion is vacuous: opus-1 2/3, 2/3, 2/3, 1/3, 2/3 passed; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 5/6, 5/6, 5/6, 4/6, 5/6; haiku-2 2/3 on all five. opus-1 checked its own mutants in memory with elixir -e, and edited its file afterwards (two test names and two comments reworded, two log assertions shortened); haiku-1's mutant write was blocked and it skipped the check, and neither left a file outside its run folder.
Against 2026-10-31 (skill): every graded rule stays clean in all five runs. other_violations goes from none to two entries, both Haiku, both layout sentences outside this case's list.
